column2: SCENARIO — Sanction received 01.04; AO authorises 15.07 (3.5 months). Consequence?

Rule: Authorisation rule: 1 MONTH authorisation (till 01.05) breached; FIRST proviso: delay BEYOND 3 MONTHS FROM CLAIM → INTEREST + the interest rule responsibility-fixing. Missing-case variant: PPO-date + 6-month bar (second proviso).

Hinglish: 1-mahina-AO-3-mahina-byaaj.

column2: SCENARIO — AO→CPAO 20 days, CPAO seal 12 days, PDA pays 20 days. Which links breached?
column3:
Rule: CPAO (10 DAYS max — the authorisation rule's sub-rule ) + PDA (15 DAYS — the authorisation rule's sub-rule ) breached; AO→CPAO within 1 MONTH (the authorisation rule's sub-rule ) ok. Relay = 1mo → 10d → 15d.

Hinglish: 1-mahina-10-din-15-din — do-tute.

column3:
Rule: authorisation ladder finds NOBODY → proviso: gratuity-nominee nephew files FORM 6 (or 6-A-instead per 2024); HoO forwards BOTH routes (forms-set OR 6-A) per with Form 7 + Format 10.

Hinglish: Koi-haqdaar-nahi to nominee-Form6.

column2: SCENARIO — Appointed 01.01.2020, takes charge 15.01.2020. QS starts?
column3:
Rule: 15.01.2020 — the qualifying-service rule: FIRST-POST CHARGE, not appointment date. 14-day gap never counts.

Hinglish: Charge-sambhalo-tab-se-gino.

Ref: Rule 11
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_11 Qualifying_Service Application CCS_Pension::Rule_11 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — 2 years officiating + then substantive appointment, continuous. Counts?
column3:
Rule: YES — qualifying-service first proviso: officiating/temporary FOLLOWED BY substantive counts. Break before substantive would kill it.

Hinglish: Officiating-pakka-jude.

Ref: Rule 11 First Proviso; Rule 11

column2: SCENARIO — Joined at 17, served 1 year pre-18 + 9 after. QS =?
column3:
Rule: 9 YEARS — qualifying-service second proviso wipes pre-18 service. 9y < 10y → service gratuity (pension rescues only 9y9m+ (verified)).

Hinglish: 18-se-pehle-shunya.

Ref: Rule 11 Second Proviso; Rule 11; Rule 44(8)

column2: SCENARIO — Dies after 6 months leave WITHOUT pay (no duties, no pay). Counts?
column3:
Rule: NO — paid-service needs DUTIES + PAY both; unpaid-idle fails. (If it were medical-EOL, leave-counting would save it — different gate.)

Hinglish: Kaam-tankhvah-dono-chahiye.

Ref: Rule 12; Rule 21(ii)
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_12 Qualifying_Service Evaluation CCS_Pension::Rule_12 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — Salary paid from a Govt-administered LOCAL FUND (not CFI). Counts?
column3:
Rule: YES — paid-service explanation: CFI OR Govt-administered Local Fund both pass the funding test.

Hinglish: Local-Fund-bhi-chalega.

Ref: Rule 12 Explanation; Rule 12

column2: SCENARIO — 5 years under a NON-CONTRIBUTORY scheme (no Govt order). Counts?
column3:
Rule: NO — paid-service explanation bars non-contributory-scheme service UNLESS Government orders otherwise (override). No order = no count.

Hinglish: Order-nahi to ginti-nahi.

Ref: Rule 12 Explanation; Rule 12

column2: SCENARIO — Centre→State PERMANENT transfer; State retires him. Who pays pension?
column3:
Rule: CENTRAL GOVERNMENT (the State-transfer rule's sub-rule ) — liability stays with Centre; State-transfer preserves counting.

Hinglish: Rajya-bhejo-Kendra-bhugto.

Ref: Rule 13(1), (3); Rule 13(1); Rule 13(3)

column2: SCENARIO — Resigns WITHOUT permission, joins State next week. QS preserved?
column3:
Rule: NO — State-transfer needs PROPER PERMISSION + Explanation's 2 conditions. Bare resignation = resignation forfeiture.

Hinglish: Bina-permission-isteefa-seva-gayi.

Ref: Rule 13(2); Rule 26(1)
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_13 Rule_26 Evaluation CCS_Pension::Rule_13 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — PSU spell claimed with permission + link but NO lump-sum refund. Counts under the PSU-counting rule?
column3:
Rule: NO — PSU-counting refund (pension/service-gratuity + retirement gratuity drawn) is MANDATORY; all 4 conditions all 4 clauses are cumulative; commutation per 1981 Table.

Hinglish: Paisa-wapas-bina-ginti-nahi.

Ref: Rule 14(1)(a)-(d); Rule 14; Rule 14(1)(c); Rule 14(a)-(d); Rule 14(d)
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_14 PSU Evaluation CCS_Pension::Rule_14 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — Casual labourer with 10y temporary status, NEVER regularised. QS?
column3:
Rule: ZERO — the temporary-status rule's 50% unlocks ONLY on REGULARISATION (Casual Labourers Scheme 1993 + DoPT). Unregularised = definition exclusion zone.

Hinglish: Regular-nahi to aadha-nahi.

Ref: Rule 15; Rule 2(b)

column2: COMPUTE — 8y temporary-status + regularised + 12y regular. QS?
column3:
Rule: 4y (50% × 8) + 12y = 16 YEARS → pension + gratuity (≥10y).

Hinglish: Aadha-jod-poora.

Ref: Rule 15

column2: SCENARIO — Probationer resigns BEFORE confirmation. Probation counts?
column3:
Rule: NO — probation needs probation + CONFIRMATION (same/another post). Unconfirmed probation dangles uncounted (+ resignation forfeiture anyway).

Hinglish: Pakki-bina-pariksha-bekaar.

Ref: Rule 16; Rule 26

column2: SCENARIO — Trade apprentice 2y, then regular appointment. Counts? SAS apprentice (IA&AD) 2y?
column3:
Rule: Trade: NO (the apprenticeship rule blanket ban). SAS-IA&AD/DAD: YES (narrow exception). Same 2 years, opposite answers.

Hinglish: Aam-apprentice-bahar, SAS-andar.

Ref: Rule 17
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_17 Exception Evaluation CCS_Pension::Rule_17 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — Contract 2001–2005 (pre-cutoff), then regularised. CPF employer share Rs 1L + interest. Counting price?
column3:
Rule: The contract-service covers pre-31.12.2003 contract; the contract-service rule's sub-rule: refund CPF GOVT contribution CUMULATIVE (1L + accrued interest). Prior SANCTION (not knowledge) is the gate-word.

Hinglish: 2003-contract-gina, CPF-byaaj-samet-wapas.

Ref: Rule 18(i), (ii); Rule 18(i); Rule 18(ii)

column2: SCENARIO — Superannuation pensioner re-employed, seeks civil-return counting. Eligible?
column3:
Rule: NO — civil-return covers ONLY compensation/invalid pension/gratuity entrants; SUPERANNUATION + RETIRING pensioners are OUTSIDE the civil-return rule (separate re-employment-pay rules).

Hinglish: Superannuation-19-me-nahi.

Trap: Entry class.

Ref: Rule 19(1); Rule 19
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_19 Re_Employment Evaluation CCS_Pension::Rule_19 Priority::Critical

column2: COMPUTE — Invalid pensioner drew pension Rs 3L + commutation Rs 2L + gratuity Rs 1L, re-employed. civil-return refund + instalments?
column3:
Rule: Refund Rs 6L total; max 36 MONTHLY instalments (the civil-return rule's sub-rule ); right revives ONLY on FULL refund; pre-re-employment pension slice stays (the civil-return rule's sub-rule (i)) but pay-fixation gratuity element returns.

Hinglish: 6L-36-kisht-poora-tab-haq.

Ref: Rule 19(2), (3); Rule 19; Rule 19(3); Rule 19(2)(i); Rule 19(2); Rule 19(ii)

column2: SCENARIO — Re-employed pensioner dies after refunding 20/36 instalments. Balance?
column3:
Rule: Civil Return rule: balance adjusted from DEATH GRATUITY payable to family. Family's gratuity shrinks by the unpaid refund.

Hinglish: Baaki-maut-gratuity-se.

Ref: Rule 19(4)

column2: SCENARIO — Ex-serviceman keeps drawing military pension AND claims civil counting of military service. Allowed?
column3:
Rule: NO — military-counting expl.2: KEEP pension = service NOT counted. Counting needs refund (pension + commutation + gratuities, the military-counting rule's sub-rule ) in ≤36 instalments (the military-counting rule's sub-rule ).

Hinglish: Fauji-pension-rakhi to ginti-gayi.

Ref: Rule 20 Expl.2; Rule 20(1), (2); Rule 20; Rule 20(1); Rule 20(2)
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_20 Military_Service Evaluation CCS_Pension::Rule_20 Priority::High

column2: APPLY — Pre-2022 advice said military gratuity 'was NOT required to be refunded'. Post-2022 answer?
column3:
Rule: REVERSED — military-counting now reads 'WAS TO BE REFUNDED' (G.S.R. 770(E)). Old advice is HISTORICAL error.

Hinglish: 2022-ulta-wapas-karo.

Ref: Rule 20 Expl.1(ii)
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_20_Exp1_ii GSR_770_E_2022 Reversal CCS_Pension::Rule_20 Priority::Critical CCS_Pension::Rule_20_Exp1_ii

column2: SCENARIO — Soldier joins civil post in 2010 (post-cutoff). military counting?
column3:
Rule: NO — military-counting expl.3: post-31.12.2003 joiners = NPS persons; NPS Rules govern, not the military-counting rule refund-and-count.

Hinglish: 2003-baad-NPS.

Ref: Rule 20 Expl.3; Rule 20

column2: SCENARIO — Military→civil with a 6-month gap; civil→civil identical gap. Condonation contrast?
column3:
Rule: Military: military-counting condonation DEEMED INCLUDED (auto). Civil: condonation rails (auto only if book silent + non-barred). Military smoother.

Hinglish: Fauji-muaafi-khud.

Ref: Rule 20(4); Rule 28
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_20 Rule_28 Comparison CCS_Pension::Rule_20 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — The civil-return rule civil + military counting pensioners retire identically. Pension-cap contrast?
column3:
Rule: Civil: civil-return caps combined outcome. Military: military-counting no LIMITATION — later civil pension runs free. Same service, different ceilings.

Hinglish: Civil-seema-fauji-khula.

Ref: Rule 19(5); Rule 20(5); Rule 19; Rule 20
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_19 Rule_20 Comparison CCS_Pension::Rule_19 Priority::Critical

column2: SCENARIO — 2y half-pay leave (with leave salary). Counts?
column3:
Rule: YES fully — the leave-counting rule's sub-rule (i): leave WITH leave salary ALWAYS counts. No conditions.

Hinglish: Tankhvah-chhutti-pakka.

Ref: Rule 21(i)

column2: SCENARIO — 1y EOL for TB treatment (medical certificate). Counts?
column3:
Rule: YES fully — the leave-counting rule's sub-rule: medical EOL ALWAYS counts.

Hinglish: Bimaari-EOL-pakka.

Ref: Rule 21(ii)

column2: SCENARIO — 2y EOL for (a) MTech, (b) MBA, (c) riot-curfew stranding. Which count?
column3:
Rule: YES (higher scientific/technical). NO (management ≠ scientific/technical). YES (civil commotion). leave-counting two grounds only.

Hinglish: MTech-haan, MBA-na, danga-haan.

Ref: Rule 21(iii); Rule 21(a); Rule 21(b); Rule 21(c)
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_21 Scenario Application CCS_Pension::Rule_21 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — Leave entry made 2 months BEFORE superannuation (years late). Valid?
column3:
Rule: NO — leave-counting explanation: late entry allowed till 6 MONTHS BEFORE superannuation. 2-month entry is time-barred; fallback: doubt favours EMPLOYEE (Govt must disprove).

Hinglish: 6-mahine-katib; shak-karmchari.

Ref: Rule 21 Explanation; Rule 21
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_21 Explanation Timeline CCS_Pension::Rule_21 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — Group C training 1y on stipend, then appointment. Group B identical training, NO Govt order. Counts?
column3:
Rule: Group C: YES (training/joining auto). Group B: NO without Government order. Rank changes the answer.

Hinglish: C-khud, B-order.

Ref: Rule 22(1), (2); Rule 22(1); Rule 22(2)

column2: SCENARIO — Joining time 12 days; servant joins on day 20 (8 days excess), no leave due. Treatment?
column3:
Rule: Training/joining rule: 12-day gap counts. the training/joining rule's sub-rule: 8-day excess → HoD-sanctioned EOL, and THIS EOL COUNTS (exception to the leave-counting rule strictness).

Hinglish: Zyada-joining-EOL-gina.

Trap: the training/joining rule's sub-rule vs the leave-counting rule.

Ref: Rule 22(3), (4); Rule 22(3); Rule 21; Rule 22(4)

column2: SCENARIO — Suspended 1y, FULLY EXONERATED, but inquiry holds suspension was JUSTIFIED. Suspension counts?
column3:
Rule: NO — suspension needs BOTH limbs (exonerated/minor-penalty AND wholly-unjustified). Justified suspension fails limb 2 despite exoneration.

Hinglish: Bari-kaafi-nahi-bevajah-bhi.

Trap: AND gate.

Ref: Rule 23(1)

column2: SCENARIO — Minor penalty (censure) + suspension held wholly unjustified + express declaration. Counts?
column3:
Rule: YES — suspension limb 1 (only minor penalty) + limb 2 (unjustified) + suspension express declaration AT THE TIME + suspension entry in EVERY case.

Hinglish: Halka-dand-bevajah-ghoshna-gina.

Ref: Rule 23(1), (2), (3); Rule 23(1); Rule 23(2); Rule 23(3)

column2: SCENARIO — Declaration under suspension made 2 years AFTER reinstatement. Valid?
column3:
Rule: NO — declaration must be AT THE TIME (contemporaneous). Belated declarations are void; suspension entry must still record the (negative) outcome.

Hinglish: Ghoshna-usi-waqt.

Ref: Rule 23(2), (3); Rule 23(2); Rule 23(3)

column2: SCENARIO — Dismissed after 15y; 5y later offence pardoned (no reinstatement). QS?
column3:
Rule: ZERO — forfeiture stands; pardon ≠ the reinstatement rule reinstatement-on-appeal/review. Only compassionate allowance allowance (≤2/3) may rescue.

Hinglish: Maafi-bahali-nahi.

Ref: Rule 24; Rule 25; Rule 41
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_24 Forfeiture Evaluation CCS_Pension::Rule_24 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — Compulsorily retired; HoO invokes forfeiture. Valid?
column3:
Rule: NO — compulsory retirement is NOT in the forfeiture rule (dismissal/removal only). compulsory-retirement pension (2/3–full) follows instead.

Hinglish: Compulsory-24-bahar-40-andar.

Trap: Classic.

Ref: Rule 24; Rule 40

column2: SCENARIO — Removed 2015, reinstated on APPEAL 2018, retired 2030. QS + gap?
column3:
Rule: Past service COUNTS (the reinstatement rule's sub-rule ); 2015–18 gap NOT counted unless REGULARISED by specific order (the reinstatement rule's sub-rule ) — reinstatement revives service, not the gap.

Hinglish: Bahali-seva-wapas-gap-alag.

Ref: Rule 25(1), (2); Rule 25(1); Rule 25(2)

column2: SCENARIO — Resigns to join SBI (no permission). Then claims resignation exception. Decide.
column3:
Rule: REJECT twice no PROPER PERMISSION bank = resignation private/body exclusion (Govt-to-Govt only). resignation forfeiture stands.

Hinglish: Bank-bina-permission-do-galti.

Ref: Rule 26(1), (2), (6); Rule 26(2); Rule 26(6); Rule 26(1)

column2: SCENARIO — Permission-route resignation; order SILENT on counting; HoO makes NO entry. Saved?
column3:
Rule: NO — resignation needs order to CLEARLY INDICATE + HoO SPECIFIC entry. Silence kills the exception; cure prospectively only (VERIFY).

Hinglish: Chup-order-entry-nahi-bacha-nahi.

Ref: Rule 26(3)

column2: SCENARIO — Resignation withdrawn AFTER acceptance, appointing authority refuses. Valid refusal?
column3:
Rule: YES — the resignation rule's sub-rule 's 4 conditions gate withdrawal (pre-acceptance + continuity + AA acceptance...); post-acceptance refusal is lawful.

Hinglish: Manzoor-ke-baad-wapsi-nahi.

Ref: Rule 26(5)

column2: SCENARIO — 10-day unauthorised absence; post NOT filled; AA later commutes it as EOL. Effect?
column3:
Rule: SAVED twice: absence covers absence-till-filled; absence retrospective EOL-commutation regularises. Either suffices.

Hinglish: Gayab-bharti-tak-EOL-baad.

Ref: Rule 27(1)(b), (2); Rule 27(1)(b); Rule 27(2)

column2: SCENARIO — Transfer to NON-qualifying post in PUBLIC INTEREST for 3y, then back. Break?
column3:
Rule: NO BREAK — absence excepts public-interest transfers; past service intact (non-qualifying spell itself doesn't accrue).

Hinglish: Jan-hit-transfer-jod-bacha.

Ref: Rule 27(1)(d)

column2: SCENARIO — 6-month private-business break (no leave, no suspension, no transfer). Condonable?
column3:
Rule: NO exception fits the absence rule's sub-rule all 5 clauses → FORFEITURE of past service. Only condonation discretion (non-barred cause) or the absence rule's sub-rule EOL-commutation could save — business-break unlikely to earn either.

Hinglish: Niji-break-paanc-me-nahi-zabt.

Ref: Rule 27; Rule 28; Rule 27(1)(a); Rule 27(2); Rule 27(a)-(e); Rule 27(1)
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_27 Forfeiture Evaluation CCS_Pension::Rule_27 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — Old 3-month gap; service book SILENT. Application needed for condonation?
column3:
Rule: NO — condonation auto-condones absent contrary indication. Gap itself unpaid (the condonation rule's sub-rule ); link bridged free.

Hinglish: Chup-kitaab-muaafi-khud.

Ref: Rule 28(1), (3); Rule 28(1); Rule 28(3)

column2: SCENARIO — Gap caused by unpunished STRIKE (book silent). Auto-condoned?
column3:
Rule: NO — condonation lists strike as a bar; silence cannot override an express bar. Same for resignation/dismissal/removal gaps.

Hinglish: Hadtaal-chaar-rok.

Ref: Rule 28(2)

column2: SCENARIO — AA refuses condonation citing 'administrative inconvenience', no hearing. Valid?
column3:
Rule: NO — the condonation rule's sub-rule: refusal ONLY in exceptional/grave circumstances + REPRESENTATION + PERSONAL HEARING mandatory. Convenience ≠ grave.

Hinglish: Sunwai-bina-mana-galat.

Ref: Rule 28(4)-(6); Rule 28(4)(6)-(6); Rule 28(4); Rule 28(6)
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_28 Procedure Evaluation CCS_Pension::Rule_28 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — 4y UN deputation; servant skips contribution, claims counting. Allowed?
column3:
Rule: NO — the UN-deputation rule: counting needs CONTRIBUTION; the -refund proviso only returns paid sums. No pay = no count.

Hinglish: UN-chanda-bina-ginti-nahi.

Ref: Rule 29; Rule 29(b)
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_29 Deputation Evaluation CCS_Pension::Rule_29 Priority::Medium

column2: SCENARIO — Servant completes 18y service; HoO skips verification ('will do at retirement'). Valid?
column3:
Rule: NO — the verification-timeline rule's sub-rule: verification AT 18 YEARS + 5-YEARS-BEFORE-superannuation, conveyed in FORMAT 4 after HoO+AO consultation. Skipping both breaches; the verification-timeline rule's sub-rule: 31-JANUARY report to Secretary tracks compliance.

Hinglish: 18-aur-5-pehle-jaanch-laazmi.

Ref: Rule 30(1), (5); Rule 30(1); Rule 30(5)
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_30 Timeline Format Evaluation CCS_Pension::Rule_30 Priority::High

column2: SCENARIO — The verification-timeline rule verification completed 2020; 2022 amendment changes counting. Reopen?
column3:
Rule: YES, narrowly — the verification-timeline rule's sub-rule: verification FINAL EXCEPT for RULE CHANGES. Amendment-driven delta reopens; fishing re-audit stays barred.

Hinglish: Niyam-badla to khula.

Ref: Rule 30(4); Rule 30

column2: SCENARIO — Department abolished; staff rendered surplus. verification timeline trigger?
column3:
Rule: YES — the verification-timeline rule's sub-rule: transfer/closure/SURPLUS events trigger verification outside the 18y/5y clocks.

Hinglish: Band-vibhaag-jaanch-turant.

Ref: Rule 30(3); Rule 30

column2: MASTER SCENARIO — Join 18 (charge day 1) → 2y probation-confirmed → 1y medical EOL → 6mo unauthorised gap (post unfilled, book silent) → 3y UN (contribution paid) → resign WITH permission to State → State service 8y → retire. Compute QS + flag each gate.
column3:
Rule: 2 + the provision rule + 0-gap-link-saved(absence/condonation, gap unpaid) + 3 + 8 = 14y countable (+ permission-route resignation saves pre-resignation). Pension (≥10y) + retirement gratuity.

Hinglish: Jod-muaafi-deputation-rajya-14-saal-pension.

Ref: Rules 11-30 synthesis; Rule 26(2); Rule 13(2); Rule 1(leave-counting)
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_11 Rule_30 Qualifying_Service Synthesis CCS_Pension::Rule_11 Priority::Critical

column2: EX1-STEP1 — Base pick: emoluments Rs 85,000 vs average Rs 82,000. Which and why?
column3:
Step: Rs 85,000 — the pension rule's sub-rule: WHICHEVER MORE BENEFICIAL. Always compute BOTH (the emoluments rule vs the average-emoluments rule) first.

Hinglish: Dono-nikaal-jo-bada.

Ref: Rule 44(1); Example 1; Rule 31; Rule 32
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_44 Worked_Example Calculation CCS_Pension::Rule_44 Priority::High

column2: EX1-STEP2 — QS 32y4m → six-monthly periods?
column3:
Step: 4m ≥ 3m → +1 period (the pension rule's sub-rule ): 64 + 1 = 65 periods = 32.5y. Rounding builds gratuity-periods AND pension-gate years alike.

Hinglish: 4-mahina-aadha-saal.

Ref: Rule 44(7); Example 1

column2: EX1-STEP3 — Pension-gate check: 32.5y → pension or service gratuity?
column3:
Step: PENSION — ≥10y (the pension rule's sub-rule ); pension near-miss unneeded. <10y would flip to pension service gratuity.

Hinglish: 10-paar-pension.

Ref: Rule 44(1), (8); Example 1; Rule 44(8); Rule 44(2)(3)-(3); Rule 44(1)

column2: EX1-STEP4 — 50% × 85,000 = 42,500: floor/ceiling/rupee checks?
column3:
Step: 9,000 ≤ 42,500 ≤ 1,25,000 ✓; the pension rule's sub-rule: already whole rupees, no change. Final: Rs 42,500/mo + DR.

Hinglish: Seema-gol-dono-paas.

Ref: Rule 44(1), (9); Example 1; Rule 44(9)

column2: EX2-STEP1 — QS 9y10m: apply the pension rule's sub-rule (8). Result?
column3:
Step: 9y10m > 9y9m → DEEMED 10y → pension-gate OPENS. Memorise: 9y9m+ = pension; 9y8m = gratuity-only.

Hinglish: 9y9m-paar-darwaza-khula.

Ref: Rule 44(8); Example 2
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_44 Near_Miss Worked_Example CCS_Pension::Rule_44 Priority::Critical

column2: EX2-STEP2 — Pension Rs 30,000: is retirement gratuity ALSO due? Compute (20 periods)?
column3:
Step: YES — addition not alternative: ¼ × 60,000 × 20 = Rs 3,00,000 (≤16.5× = 9.9L ✓; ≤25L ✓).

Hinglish: Pension-saath-gratuity.

Ref: Rule 45(1)(a); Example 2

column2: EX3-STEP1 — Age 82 → which pension slab and base?
column3:
Step: 80–85 → 20% ON BASIC pension (Rs 30,000), NOT on basic+DR. Base error = classic trap.

Hinglish: Basic-par-20.

Ref: Rule 44(6); Example 3
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_44 Additional_Pension Worked_Example CCS_Pension::Rule_44 Priority::High

column2: EX3-STEP2 — Additional Rs 6,000: effective from + DR treatment?
column3:
Step: From 1ST OF BIRTH-MONTH; total Rs 36,000 + DR 60% on (basic + additional) = Rs 21,600 → Rs 57,600/mo.

Hinglish: Mahine-pehli-se-DR-sab-par.

Ref: Rule 44(6); Rule 52; Example 3
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_44 Dearness_Relief Worked_Example CCS_Pension::Rule_44 Priority::High

column2: EX4-STEP1 — QS 6mo / 3y: slab multiples?
column3:
Step: <1y → 2×; 1–5y → 6×. Early-career deaths use FLAT multiples, not half-month math.

Hinglish: Chhoti-seva-flat-guna.

Ref: Rule 45(1)(b); Example 4
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_45 Death_Gratuity Worked_Example CCS_Pension::Rule_45 Priority::High

column2: EX4-STEP2 — QS 7y / 15y: slab multiples + 11y-boundary logic?
column3:
Step: 5–11y → 12×; 11–20y → 20×. Exactly-11y falls in 20× band (upper band owns the boundary).

Hinglish: 11-20guna-seema-upar.

Ref: Rule 45(1)(b); Example 4
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_45 Death_Gratuity Worked_Example CCS_Pension::Rule_45 Priority::High

column2: EX4-STEP3 — QS 25y (50 periods): arithmetic + 33× check?
column3:
Step: ½ × 70,000 × 50 = 25× = Rs 17.5L ≤ 33× ✓. 20y+ uses HALF-MONTH math (like service gratuity), not flat multiples.

Hinglish: 20-paar-aadha-mahina.

Ref: Rule 45(1)(b); Example 4
column5: CCS_Pension Rule_45 Death_Gratuity Worked_Example CCS_Pension::Rule_45 Priority::High

column2: EX4-STEP4 — Base + overall cap order for all five cases?
column3:
